episode.title: Honor server retry advice without restarting its countdown
episode.before: At parent ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, HTTP retry loops ignored Retry-After and always used local exponential backoff. Retry delays carried by higher-level errors were relative durations, so time spent reading bodies, mapping errors, emitting notifications, or otherwise propagating an error could restart or extend the server-requested wait. Expired server advice was therefore indistinguishable from missing advice and could incorrectly fall back to local backoff.
episode.after: At 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, retry advice is parsed when received into a monotonic absolute deadline supporting delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms. That deadline is attached to transport and semantic errors, retained through API and provider mappings and exhausted retry state, and used by HTTP and stream retry loops with sleep-until semantics. Invalid or absent advice still uses local backoff; explicit zero or expired valid advice remains present as a zero remaining delay.
episode.diff: The change adds the RetryAfter deadline value and parser; captures it from unsuccessful HTTP response headers before body processing; replaces relative retry-delay fields across transport, API, provider, protocol, and streaming layers; makes request and stream retries wait for the original deadline while retaining local backoff as the no-advice fallback; and adds unit, mapping, virtual-time, and end-to-end tests for parsing, countdown, expiry, delayed notification, exhausted retries, and successful recovery. The commit changes 28 files with 429 insertions and 86 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331 with parent ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2; its commit message states that HTTP retries used local backoff despite Retry-After and relative delays failed to account for propagation and reporting time.
The commit modifies 28 files with 429 insertions and 86 deletions, spanning HTTP transport, request retries, API/error mappings, stream retry state, provider adaptation, and tests.

RetryAfter stores a monotonic Instant, parses nonnegative delta-seconds or an HTTP date, exposes the original deadline, and computes a saturating remaining delay so expired advice remains zero rather than becoming absent.
Both buffered and streaming HTTP transport paths parse Retry-After from response headers as soon as an unsuccessful response arrives and attach the captured deadline to TransportError::Http.
The HTTP retry loop prefers the attached server deadline, records its current remaining delay, sleeps until the absolute deadline, and uses jittered local backoff only when advice is absent.

API error mapping extracts RetryAfter before changing the semantic error variant and reattaches the same value afterward, preserving advice across retryable, rate-limit, overload, and HTTP transport mappings.

CodexErr now retains RetryAfter, derives remaining server delay from its original deadline, distinguishes expired valid advice from missing advice, and continues to apply retryability and retry-budget policy independently of the presence of advice.

The stream retry handler retains the original server deadline across asynchronous user notification, sleeps until that deadline, and stores it when stream retries are exhausted; the special unbounded connection-retry and transport-fallback branches retain their separate policies.

Parser tests prove delta-seconds count down to zero, HTTP dates map to the monotonic clock, explicit zero and past dates remain valid zero-delay advice, and malformed or overflowing values are rejected.
A virtual-time stream test delays retry notification and proves the retry still resumes at the originally captured deadline rather than waiting a fresh relative duration.
An integration test serves a 503 with Retry-After: 1, observes HTTP-layer retry telemetry, verifies at least one second elapses before retry, and confirms recovery with exactly two response requests.

A virtual-time integration test proves the final HTTP retry error retains its later server deadline through API mapping, reports the decreasing remaining delay, and still reports Some(Duration::ZERO) after expiry.
Provider-specific error rewriting is tested to preserve the original retry deadline rather than replacing it while changing the user-facing error details.
The parent implementation contained an explicit TODO in the HTTP retry loop and always selected local backoff before sleeping for a relative delay.

candidate_atomics.name: capture-server-retry-deadline
candidate_atomics.title: Capture server retry advice as an absolute deadline
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize valid relative-seconds or HTTP-date retry advice at receipt time into one monotonic deadline, while preserving the distinction between missing, invalid, expired, and explicit-zero advice.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent server-requested retry timing from being restarted or lengthened by subsequent processing.
semantic_action.pre_state: An unsuccessful response has arrived with optional raw retry-advice headers or an equivalent streamed delay signal.
semantic_action.post_state: Valid advice is represented by one monotonic deadline captured at receipt; expired or zero advice remains present with zero remaining delay, while invalid or absent advice produces no deadline.
semantic_action.validation: Use paused-time parser tests to verify delta-seconds countdown, HTTP-date conversion, zero and expired values, and rejection of malformed or overflowing values.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-retry-deadline-through-error-mapping
candidate_atomics.title: Preserve retry deadlines through error translation
candidate_atomics.description: Carry the same captured deadline through transport, API, provider, protocol, and exhausted-retry representations even when the semantic error type or user-facing message changes.

semantic_action.intent: Keep retry timing stable while errors cross abstraction and provider boundaries.
semantic_action.pre_state: A lower-layer error contains a captured retry deadline and must be translated, reclassified, reworded, or retained after a retry budget is exhausted.
semantic_action.post_state: The translated or retained error exposes the identical original deadline; its remaining duration decreases with elapsed time and reaches zero without becoming absent.
semantic_action.validation: Map errors after virtual time advances and assert deadline identity, decreasing remaining delay, zero-after-expiry behavior, and preservation through provider-specific rewriting and exhausted retry state.

candidate_atomics.name: schedule-retry-against-preserved-deadline
candidate_atomics.title: Schedule retries against the preserved deadline
candidate_atomics.description: For retryable failures within budget, wait until the server's absolute deadline when present and otherwise retain the established local-backoff policy; compute telemetry from the remaining wait after intervening work.

semantic_action.intent: Honor upstream timing without changing retry eligibility, retry budgets, fallback behavior, or the no-advice backoff policy.
semantic_action.pre_state: A failure is independently classified as retryable, retry budget remains, and the error may or may not contain a server deadline.
semantic_action.post_state: Advice-bearing retries resume no earlier than the original deadline despite propagation or notification time; retries without advice use local backoff; terminal errors and exhausted budgets remain terminal under existing policy.
semantic_action.validation: Verify end-to-end HTTP recovery and request count, paused-time fallback backoff, delayed stream notification against the original deadline, and retained advice after HTTP retry exhaustion.

candidate_workflows.name: honor-server-retry-deadlines-across-layered-recovery
candidate_workflows.title: Honor server retry deadlines across layered recovery
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for systems where retry advice crosses transport, semantic-error, provider, and streaming boundaries before the next attempt is scheduled.

workflow_graph.goal: Make every eligible retry honor the server's originally requested earliest retry time without restarting the countdown during error propagation and without replacing established retry policy when advice is unavailable.
when_to_use: A client receives retry timing from HTTP headers or streamed errors but currently retries using only local backoff.
Retry advice passes through multiple error mappings, notifications, provider adapters, or exhausted-retry state before reuse.
Observed retry waits begin too late because each layer stores or reconstructs a relative duration.
anti_goals: Do not make terminal failures retryable merely because they carry retry advice.
Do not expand configured retry budgets or remove existing transport-fallback and unbounded connection-retry policies.
Do not replace local backoff for failures with missing or invalid server advice.
Do not treat an expired valid deadline as missing advice and introduce a new backoff delay.
not_applicable_when: The upstream protocol supplies no retry timing and local backoff is already the intended complete policy.
The operation is not safely retryable or retry eligibility cannot be established independently of timing advice.
Retry timing never crosses an asynchronous or abstraction boundary and an existing absolute-deadline representation is already preserved end to end.
inputs: Raw server retry-advice headers or streamed delay signal
Clock facilities supporting a monotonic deadline
Transport and semantic error types crossed by the failure
Retry eligibility rules and configured retry budgets
Request and stream retry call sites
Deterministic clock-controlled and end-to-end recovery tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: Retryable failures may contain server advice, but request retries ignore it or higher layers carry relative durations that can restart during propagation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Valid advice is captured once, preserved unchanged across all relevant error boundaries, and consumed as an absolute deadline by eligible retry schedulers; invalid or absent advice uses local backoff, while zero or expired valid advice produces an immediate eligible retry rather than fallback delay.

steps.condition: Required when the failure source can provide server retry timing.
steps.validation: Parser and transport tests establish accepted formats, receipt-time capture, countdown, expiry, and invalid-value behavior.

steps.condition: Required for every error translation, reclassification, provider rewrite, or exhausted-retry record between receipt and scheduling.
steps.validation: Mapping tests assert the same deadline survives translation and its remaining delay continues to decrease through elapsed virtual time.

steps.condition: Required only after existing policy independently declares the failure retryable and budget remains; use local backoff when no valid deadline exists.
steps.validation: Virtual-time and end-to-end tests prove sleep-until behavior, delayed-notification accounting, local-backoff fallback, bounded attempts, telemetry, and successful recovery.

validation_ladder: Unit-test parsing of delta-seconds, HTTP dates, explicit zero, expired dates, malformed values, and overflow.
Test transport capture before body processing and verify advice is attached to unsuccessful-response errors.
Test each error-mapping boundary for deadline identity and decreasing remaining duration.
Use paused time to prove intervening notification or propagation work consumes the original wait rather than preceding a fresh delay.
Verify no-advice failures still use bounded jittered backoff and retry eligibility remains independent of advice.
Run end-to-end recovery with a mock server, retry telemetry, elapsed-time assertion, successful completion, and exact request count.
Exercise retry exhaustion and confirm the last captured deadline remains available and becomes zero rather than absent after expiry.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the response-arrival boundary cannot be identified reliably enough to capture advice once.
Stop if retryability or idempotency is unresolved; timing advice alone must not authorize another attempt.
Stop if an error-mapping boundary drops metadata and cannot be changed or tested without altering a public compatibility contract.
Stop when retry budget is exhausted or the existing policy classifies the error as terminal, while retaining advice only if downstream recovery state explicitly requires it.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation leaves a TODO for honoring server advice before switching from WebSockets to fallback HTTP transport.
The buffered execute path notes that retry advice is not preserved when unbounded diagnostic-body reading itself fails with a network or timeout classification.
Wrapped WebSocket HTTP errors introduced in this change still populate retry_after as None rather than parsing their available headers.

unresolved_questions: No GitHub issue body, comments, review discussion, or status-check evidence was available; repository code, tests, commit metadata, and the supplied bundle establish the episode.
The checkout working tree contains broad pre-existing deletions, so extraction used pinned git objects and parent-to-commit diffs without modifying or relying on the working tree.
